# Statistical Outputs and Model Parameters

This appendix collects the full statistical output of the integrated step-selection function and the parameter settings of the five plugin analysis modules, so that the results in the main text can be reproduced and audited.

## Final iSSF Coefficients

The final conditional logistic regression was fitted on 7,824 in-matrix transit steps from 14 GPS-collared individuals in Canton Aargau, each compared against ten random control steps. All covariates are z-standardised with the Aargau training mean and standard deviation. The seven retained coefficients, are summarised here for reference: distance to railway ($\hat{\beta} = 0.485$), forest density at the 50-metre scale ($\hat{\beta} = 0.518$), forest density gradient at the 1000-metre scale ($\hat{\beta} = 0.235$), distance to main road ($\hat{\beta} = 0.277$), distance to settlement ($\hat{\beta} = 0.225$), distance to secondary road ($\hat{\beta} = 0.164$), and distance to water ($\hat{\beta} = 0.056$). All coefficients were positive and significant at the 0.05 level, and the variance inflation factors for the retained set ranged from 1.08 to 1.49.

## Variable Selection Record

| Covariate | Decision | Reason |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Forest density 50 m | Retained | Strongest selection signal |
| Forest density gradient 1000 m | Retained | Macro-scale habitat context |
| Distance to water | Retained | Weak but significant |
| Distance to main road | Retained | Infrastructure avoidance |
| Distance to secondary road | Retained | Infrastructure avoidance |
| Distance to settlement | Retained | Infrastructure avoidance |
| Distance to railway | Retained | Strong avoidance, wider CI |
| Binary forest cover | Removed | Redundant with density layers |
| Distance to forest edge | Removed | Redundant with density layers |
| Slope | Removed | VIF \> 80 with TRI, non-significant |
| Terrain Ruggedness Index | Removed | VIF \> 80 with slope, non-significant |
| Distance to flowing water | Removed | Collinear with combined distance to water |
| Distance to lakes | Removed | Collinear with combined distance to water |
| Distance to fenced road | Removed | Barrier-trapping artifact ($\hat{\beta} = -0.374$) |

: Variable selection decisions for the iSSF covariate set.

## Plugin Analysis Parameters

The five analytical modules of the *Wildboar Connectivity (ASF)* plugin share one analysis window and run on the following fixed default parameters. The window extends 11,500 metres in each direction from the outbreak origin, combining a 10,000-metre buffer with a 1,500-metre edge buffer. The infection-risk kernel rescales the published mean natal dispersal distance of European wild boar, 4 kilometres, into the cost-distance surface, mapping the EFSA protection zone (3 km) and surveillance zone (10 km) onto risk thresholds of 0.50 and 0.15. The biased correlated random walk releases 500 walkers by default, each taking up to 2,000 steps with a von Mises directional concentration of $\kappa = 2.0$. The iSSF-based individual movement model runs 2,000 agents by default. Each agent draws its infectious period from a $\text{Gamma}(\alpha = 3, \beta = 3.5\,\text{days})$ distribution with a mean of 10.5 days, and at every move it evaluates 25 candidate endpoints generated from a gamma step-length kernel (shape 2.669, scale 160 m) and a von Mises turning-angle kernel ($\kappa = 1.073$).

## Reproducing the Statistical Output

The iSSF coefficient table, the step classification counts, and all covariate summary statistics reported in the results chapter are produced directly from the processed data files by the R code chunks embedded in `5-ergebnisse.qmd`. Running the Quarto document against the processed data directory regenerates every table and figure deterministically.
